sentences.en: Body language and mind.
sentences.zh: 肢体语言与心智。
sentences.asr_text: Body language and mind.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Good morning everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: In today’s lecture, I’d like to focus on how our body language reveals who we are.
sentences.zh: 今天这堂课，我想重点谈谈肢体语言如何揭示我们是怎样的人。

sentences.en: We are really fascinated with body language and particularly interested in other people’s body language.
sentences.zh: 我们对肢体语言十分着迷，尤其关注别人的肢体语言。

sentences.en: You know, we are sometimes interested in an awkward interaction, or a smile, or a contemptuous glance, or maybe a very awkward wink or handshake.
sentences.zh: 有时，一个尴尬的互动、一个微笑、一道轻蔑的目光，或是一个很不自然的眨眼、握手，都会引起我们的兴趣。

sentences.en: So, what kind of body language am I talking about?
sentences.zh: 那么，我要谈的是哪种肢体语言呢？

sentences.en: I am interested in power dynamics.
sentences.zh: 我关注的是权力关系的变化。

sentences.en: That is the non-verbal expressions of power and dominance.
sentences.zh: 也就是权力和支配地位的非语言表达。

sentences.en: And what are nonverbal expressions of power and dominance?
sentences.zh: 那么，权力和支配地位有哪些非语言表达呢？

sentences.en: Well, this is what they are: in the animal kingdom, non-verbal expressions of power and dominance are about expanding.
sentences.zh: 是这样的：在动物世界里，权力和支配地位的非语言表达，表现为身体向外扩张。

sentences.en: So, you make yourself big, you stretch out, you take up space and you are basically opening up.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你让自己显得高大，伸展身体，占据空间，基本上就是把身体打开。

sentences.en: And, and humans do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 人类也有同样的表现。

sentences.en: So, they do this when they are feeling powerful in the moment.
sentences.zh: 当人们在某一刻感觉自己有力量时，就会这样做。

sentences.en: And this one is especially interesting because it really shows us how universal and old these expressions of power are.
sentences.zh: 这种表现尤其有趣，因为它确实让我们看到，这些表达力量的动作有多么普遍，历史又有多么久远。

sentences.en: For example, when athletes cross the finish line and they’ve won, it doesn’t matter if they’ve never seen anyone do it.
sentences.zh: 例如，运动员冲过终点、赢得比赛时，哪怕从没见过别人这么做，也一样会做出这种动作。

sentences.en: They do this: so, the arms are up in a ‘V’ sign, the chin is slightly lifted.
sentences.zh: 他们会这样：双臂向上举成V字，下巴微微抬起。

sentences.en: But what do we do when we feel powerless?
sentences.zh: 可是，当我们感觉自己没有力量时，又会怎么做呢？

sentences.en: We do exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我们的做法恰好相反。

sentences.en: We close up.
sentences.zh: 我们会收拢身体。

sentences.en: We make ourselves small.
sentences.zh: 让自己显得更小。

sentences.en: We don’t want to bump into the person next to us.
sentences.zh: 我们不想碰到旁边的人。

sentences.en: And this is what happens when you put together high and low power.
sentences.zh: 当强势者和弱势者处在一起时，就会出现这样的情况。

sentences.en: So, what we tend to do when it comes to power is that we complement the other’s non-verbals.
sentences.zh: 因此，在权力关系中，我们往往会用与对方互补的非语言动作来回应。

sentences.en: What I mean is, if someone is being really powerful with us, we tend to make ourselves smaller.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果有人对我们表现得很强势，我们往往会让自己的身体缩得更小。

sentences.en: We don’t mirror them.
sentences.zh: 我们不会模仿对方的动作。

sentences.en: We do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我们会作出相反的反应。

sentences.en: I am watching this behavior in the classroom and guess what I have noticed.
sentences.zh: 我一直在课堂上观察这种行为，猜猜我发现了什么。

sentences.en: I noticed that MBA students really exhibit the full range of power non-verbals.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，MBA学生的表现几乎涵盖了从强势到弱势的全部非语言动作。

sentences.en: They get right into the middle of the room before class even starts like they really want to occupy space.
sentences.zh: 有些学生在上课前就径直走到教室中央，好像非常想占据空间。

sentences.en: When they sit down, they are sort of spread out.
sentences.zh: 坐下时，他们的身体也舒展开来。

sentences.en: They raise their hands high.
sentences.zh: 他们举手也举得很高。

sentences.en: You have other people who are virtually collapsing when they come in, as soon as they, I mean other people come in.
sentences.zh: 另一些人进来时，身体却几乎是蜷缩着的；当他们——我是说，那些人——走进教室时，就是这样。

sentences.en: You see it, you see it on their faces and their bodies and they sit with their chairs and they make themselves tiny.
sentences.zh: 你能从他们的表情和身体姿态看出来；他们坐在椅子上，尽量让自己显得很小。

sentences.en: And they will not fully stretch their arms when they raise their hands.
sentences.zh: 而且举手时，他们也不会完全伸直手臂。

sentences.en: I also notice another interesting thing about this.
sentences.zh: 我还注意到了另一个有趣的现象。

sentences.en: It seems women are much more likely to do this kind of thing than men.
sentences.zh: 女性似乎比男性更容易表现出这种姿态。

sentences.en: I mean women are more likely to make themselves small.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，女性更容易让自己显得弱小。

sentences.en: Women feel chronically less powerful than men.
sentences.zh: 女性长期以来感受到的力量往往少于男性。

sentences.en: So, this is not surprising.
sentences.zh: 因此，这并不让人惊讶。

sentences.en: The second question concerns our minds.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题涉及我们的心理。

sentences.en: We know that our minds change our bodies, but is it also true that our bodies change our minds?
sentences.zh: 我们知道，心理会改变身体；但身体也会改变心理，这同样成立吗？

sentences.en: And when I say minds in the case of the powerful, what do I mean?
sentences.zh: 谈到强势者的“心理”时，我指的是什么呢？

sentences.en: I am talking about thoughts and feelings and the sorts of physiological things that make up our thoughts and feelings, and in my case, that’s hormones.
sentences.zh: 我说的是思想、感受，以及构成这些思想和感受的各种生理因素；在我的研究中，具体就是激素。

sentences.en: I look at hormones.
sentences.zh: 我研究激素。

sentences.en: So, what do the minds of the powerful versus the powerless look like?
sentences.zh: 那么，强势者和弱势者的心理分别是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: Powerful people tend to be not surprisingly more assertive and more confident, more optimistic.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，强势者往往更果断、更自信，也更乐观。

w.m: adj.坚定自信的；敢于表达的

sentences.en: They actually feel that they’re going to win, even at games of chance.
sentences.zh: 即使是在靠运气取胜的游戏中，他们也真的觉得自己会赢。

w.m: phr.靠运气决定输赢的游戏

sentences.en: They also tend to be able to think more abstractly.
sentences.zh: 他们也往往更能进行抽象思考。

sentences.en: They take more risks.
sentences.zh: 他们更愿意冒险。

sentences.en: So, there are a lot of differences between powerful and powerless people.
sentences.zh: 因此，强势者与弱势者之间存在许多差异。

sentences.en: Physiologically, there are also differences on two key hormones.
sentences.zh: 从生理上看，两种关键激素的水平也有所不同。

sentences.en: One is dominance hormone and the other is stress hormone.
sentences.zh: 一种是支配激素，另一种是压力激素。

sentences.en: What we find is that powerful and effective leaders have high dominance hormone and low stress hormone.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，强势且高效的领导者，支配激素水平高，压力激素水平低。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: That means power is also about how you react to stress.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，力量也体现在你如何应对压力上。

sentences.en: Once we did an experiment, we decided to bring people into the lab and run that little experiment.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我们做了一项实验，把参与者请到实验室，开展了这个小实验。

sentences.en: These people adopted for two minutes either high power poses or low power poses.
sentences.zh: 这些人分别保持强势姿势或弱势姿势两分钟。

sentences.en: We, for two minutes, say “You need to do this or this”.
sentences.zh: 在这两分钟里，我们告诉他们：“你需要这样做，或者那样做。”

sentences.en: And we also want them to be feeling power.
sentences.zh: 我们也希望他们能切实感受到力量。

sentences.en: So after two minutes we will ask them “How powerful do you feel?” on a series of items and then we give them an opportunity to gamble.
sentences.zh: 两分钟后，我们通过一组题目询问他们：“你感觉自己有多强大？”随后给他们一个参与赌博的机会。

sentences.en: Before and after the experiment we take their samples of saliva for a hormone test.
sentences.zh: 实验前后，我们采集他们的唾液样本，检测激素水平。

sentences.en: That’s the whole experiment.
sentences.zh: 整个实验就是这样。

sentences.en: And this is what we have found: risk tolerance which is gambling.
sentences.zh: 以下是我们的发现：首先是风险承受度，也就是参与赌博的意愿。

sentences.en: What we find is that when you’re in the higher power pose condition, 86% of you will gamble.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，保持强势姿势时，有86%的人会选择参与赌博。

sentences.en: When you’re in the low power pose condition, it’s down to only 60%, and that’s a pretty significant difference.
sentences.zh: 而保持弱势姿势时，这一比例降到了仅60%，这个差异相当显著。

sentences.en: Here’s what we find on dominance hormone: from their baseline when they come in, high power people experience about a 20% increase and low power people experience about a 10% decrease.
sentences.zh: 在支配激素方面，我们发现：与进入实验室时的基线水平相比，强势姿势组大约上升了20%，弱势姿势组则大约下降了10%。

sentences.en: So again, two minutes and you get these changes.
sentences.zh: 所以，再强调一次，只用两分钟就能产生这些变化。

sentences.en: Concerning stress hormone high power people experience about a 25% decrease and the low power people experience about a 15% increase.
sentences.zh: 至于压力激素，强势姿势组的水平大约下降了25%，弱势姿势组则大约上升了15%。

sentences.en: Once again, two minutes led to these hormonal changes that configure your brain to basically be either assertive, confident or really stress-reactive.
sentences.zh: 同样，只用两分钟就产生了这些激素变化，使大脑进入果断、自信，或者对压力高度敏感的状态。

w.m: adj.容易对压力产生反应的

sentences.en: And you know feeling sort of shut down and we’ve all had that feeling, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种有些封闭、退缩的感觉；我们都曾有过，对吧？

sentences.en: So, it seems that our non-verbals do govern how we think and feel about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，非语言行为似乎确实会影响我们如何看待自己，以及对自己的感受。

sentences.en: Also, our bodies change our minds.
sentences.zh: 而且，身体会改变心理。

sentences.en: So, power-posing for a few minutes really changes your life in meaningful ways.
sentences.zh: 因此，做几分钟强势姿势，的确能够以有意义的方式改变生活。

sentences.en: When I tell people about this that our bodies change our minds, and our minds can change our behavior, and our behavior can change our outcomes, they say to me “I don’t believe that. It feels fake, right?”
sentences.zh: 当我告诉人们，身体能改变心理，心理能改变行为，行为又能改变结果时，他们会说：“我不相信。这感觉很假，对吧？”

sentences.en: So, I said, “fake it till you make it”.
sentences.zh: 所以我说：“先做出那个样子，直到真正做到。”

w.h: fake it till you make it
w.m: phr.先做出样子，直到真正做到

sentences.en: I’m going to leave you with this.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想留给大家这样一个建议。

sentences.en: Before you go into the next stressful evaluative situation, for example, a job interview.
sentences.zh: 在下一次进入需要接受评价、又充满压力的场合之前，比如参加求职面试之前，

sentences.en: For two minutes, try doing this, in the elevator or at your desk behind closed doors, and say to yourself “That’s what I want to do”.
sentences.zh: 试着花两分钟做这些动作，可以在电梯里，也可以在关上门的办公桌前；对自己说：“这就是我要做的。”

sentences.en: Configure your brain to do the best in that situation, get your dominance hormone up, and get your stress hormone down.
sentences.zh: 让大脑调整到能在那种情境中发挥最佳水平的状态，提高支配激素水平，降低压力激素水平。

sentences.en: Don’t leave that situation feeling like “Oh, I didn’t show them who I am”.
sentences.zh: 不要离开那个场合时还觉得：“唉，我没能让他们看到真正的我。”

sentences.en: Leave that situation feeling like “Oh, I really managed to say who I am and show who I am”.
sentences.zh: 离开时，要觉得：“我确实说清了自己是谁，也展示了真正的自己。”

sentences.en: To sum up, today we talked about the nonverbal expressions of power and dominance, and the strong effects of the change of behavior.
sentences.zh: 总结一下，今天我们谈了权力和支配地位的非语言表达，以及行为变化所带来的强烈影响。

sentences.en: I suggest you try power-posing which is simple but will significantly change the outcomes of your life.
sentences.zh: 我建议大家试试强势姿势；它很简单，却能显著改变你人生中的结果。

sentences.en: OK, next time we are going to discuss the social functions of body language.
sentences.zh: 好，下一次我们将讨论肢体语言的社会功能。

sentences.en: Now, you have three minutes to check your work.
sentences.zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。
sentences.asr_text: now, you have three minutes to check your work.
sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.zh: A节短讲到此结束。

sentences.en: Hey, Kathy.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 嘿，凯西。

sentences.en: Did you read this article in the magazine?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你看过杂志上的这篇文章了吗？

sentences.en: I can’t believe how much man’s changing the planet.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信，人类对地球的改变竟然这么大。

sentences.en: Yeah, I had a look at it.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 嗯，我看过了。

sentences.en: Quite interesting I suppose if you believe that sort of thing.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你相信这类事情的话，那倒挺有意思。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: What do you mean “if you believe that sort of thing?”
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你说“如果你相信这类事情”，是什么意思？

sentences.en: Are you saying you don’t believe that we are damaging the planet?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你是说，你不相信我们正在破坏地球吗？

sentences.en: To be honest, Mark, not really.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 说实话，马克，我不太相信。

sentences.en: What are you saying?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你在说什么？

sentences.en: Are you saying global warming isn’t a fact?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你是说，全球变暖不是事实？

sentences.en: Deforestation isn’t a fact?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 森林砍伐也不是事实？

sentences.en: The greenhouse effect isn’t actually happening?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 温室效应也并没有真的发生？

sentences.en: Hey, calm down Mark.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 嘿，马克，冷静一点。

sentences.en: I just think too many people take these things as being definitely true without knowing all the facts.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，有太多人还没了解全部事实，就认定这些事绝对是真的。

sentences.en: You really don’t think global warming is happening.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你真的认为全球变暖并没有发生？

sentences.en: You know they’ve said sea levels are going to rise by quite a few meters over the next 50 to 100 years.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们说未来50到100年，海平面将会上升好几米。

sentences.en: Weather conditions are getting worse all over the world.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 世界各地的天气状况都在恶化。

sentences.en: Can you remember how many big hurricanes there have been in this country over the last few years?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你还记得过去几年，我们国家遭遇了多少次强飓风吗？

sentences.en: I think evidence is all around us.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我觉得证据就在我们身边。

sentences.en: I don’t think we have enough information, to be honest.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 说实话，我认为我们的信息还不够充分。

sentences.en: We’ve only been measuring these things for around two or three hundred years.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们对这些现象进行测量，不过也就两三百年。

sentences.en: We have no idea what was happening 50,000 years ago.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 五万年前发生过什么，我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: For all we know, this is just a natural blip, a kind of sudden but temporary change, in the whole climate cycle.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 说不定，这只是整个气候周期中一次自然的小波动，也就是一种突然而短暂的变化。

w.m: phr.说不定；或许（表示没有足够信息作判断）

sentences.en: I don’t think we should change how we’re living just because of 20 years of abnormal measurements.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我不认为，我们仅仅因为二十年的异常测量数据，就应该改变自己的生活方式。

sentences.en: And don’t you think all the other effects we’re having on the planet are destructive?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，你不认为我们对地球造成的其他种种影响也具有破坏性吗？

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 你指的是什么？

sentences.en: I mean like deforestation, overpopulation, threatening the existence of many endangered animals.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 比如森林砍伐、人口过剩，以及威胁许多濒危动物的生存。

sentences.en: Pollution of the air and the seas.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 还有对空气和海洋的污染。

sentences.en: I mean, I could go on if you want.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，我还可以继续列举。

sentences.en: No, no, I understand what you’re saying.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 不，不，我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: And, yes, it’s true that there are several problems worldwide caused by human influence.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 而且，没错，世界各地的确有一些问题是人类活动造成的。

sentences.en: I think the destruction of the Amazon rainforest is really dangerous and it’s something we could live to regret.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我认为，亚马孙雨林遭到破坏确实很危险，将来我们可能会为此后悔。

sentences.en: I read somewhere that they were considered to be the lungs of the planet.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我曾在哪里读到过，它被称为地球之肺。

w.m: n.肺；此处比喻重要的生态调节者

sentences.en: And there we are happily chopping it all down and it would be a shame to lose some of those animals that may become extinct.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 可我们却还高高兴兴地把它砍掉；还有，失去一些可能灭绝的动物也很可惜。

sentences.en: You know, like the rhino or the panda.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 比如犀牛或熊猫。

sentences.en: But I think we shouldn’t interfere with nature if they are going to become extinct.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 不过我认为，我们不该干涉自然；如果这些动物将要灭绝，

sentences.en: Then we have to allow nature to take its course.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 那我们就得让自然顺其发展。

sentences.en: You’ve just contradicted yourself in two sentences Kathy.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 凯西，你前后两句话就自相矛盾了。

sentences.en: First you said it’s bad that we’re interfering with nature by destroying the rainforest, and then......
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你先说，我们破坏雨林、干涉自然是件坏事，然后又……

sentences.en: That’s not the same thing.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 那不是一回事。

sentences.en: Well of course it is.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 怎么不是一回事，当然是！

sentences.en: The only reason 99% of these animals are endangered is precisely because WE are threatening their habitats either by chopping it down as you say, or by expanding towns and farming into areas where these animals normally live and hunt.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 这些动物中99%之所以濒危，恰恰就是因为我们在威胁它们的栖息地：要么像你说的那样砍掉森林，要么把城镇和农田扩展到它们原本生活、觅食的地方。

sentences.en: You can’t destroy an animal’s habitat and then turn around and say we can’t interfere with nature to save it.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你不能先破坏动物的栖息地，然后掉过头来说，不能为了拯救它们而干涉自然。

sentences.en: I don’t think having 20 panda cubs in zoos around the world is a very smart way to save an animal.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我不认为，在世界各地的动物园里养二十只熊猫幼崽，就是拯救一种动物的明智办法。

sentences.en: It’s totally artificial and is cruel to the animals involved.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 那完全是人为的，对涉及其中的动物也很残忍。

sentences.en: I would go along with that.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 这一点我赞同。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The real solution is to save the animals’ original habitat.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 真正的解决办法是保护这些动物原本的栖息地。

sentences.zh: 第一段访谈到此结束。

sentences.speaker: announcer

sentences.en: Cindy, you’ve been doing research on disciplinary literacy for about 20 years now.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 辛迪，你研究学科读写素养已经大约二十年了。

sentences.en: In that time you’ve probably been asked just about everything possible.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 这些年里，你大概已经被问过几乎所有能想到的问题。

sentences.en: What question comes up most often these days?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 最近，哪一个问题被问得最多？

sentences.en: That’s easy.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这个很容易回答。

sentences.en: We are doing better convincing teachers that disciplinary literacy is worth teaching, but they still are hesitant about their students’ reactions.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们越来越能说服教师，学科读写素养值得教授，但他们仍然对学生会如何反应心存顾虑。

sentences.en: A teacher said to me recently I have enough trouble getting my kids to read a textbook chapter.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 最近，一位教师对我说：“光是让学生读完一章教科书，我就已经够费劲了。”

sentences.en: How would I ever motivate them to read in a disciplinary way?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: “我又该怎样激励他们，以学科特有的方式去阅读呢？”

sentences.en: Is that a real question or is it just a mask for teacher resistance.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 这是真正的疑问，还是掩饰教师抵触心理的借口？

sentences.en: I think it’s a real question.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我认为这是真实的疑问。

sentences.en: And in fact, it is also our biggest problem because many teachers still don’t understand the distinctions between content area reading and disciplinary literacy.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 而且，这实际上也是我们最大的问题，因为许多教师仍然不理解学科内容阅读与学科读写素养之间的区别。

sentences.en: What is disciplinary literacy anyway?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，学科读写素养究竟是什么？

sentences.en: You said that’s different.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你刚才说，它们是不一样的。

sentences.en: Disciplinary literacy doesn’t promise to make someone a better student.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 学科读写素养并不承诺把一个人变成更优秀的学生。

sentences.en: It invites students to join the disciplinary field itself.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 它邀请学生加入这个学科领域本身。

sentences.en: It’s a kind of invitation to join a club.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这就像邀请你加入一个俱乐部。

sentences.en: Does it mean it invites students to join the history club by reading like a historian or the science club by reading like a scientist?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它邀请学生像历史学家一样阅读，加入“历史俱乐部”；或者像科学家一样阅读，加入“科学俱乐部”，是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But it goes beyond that.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 但它的意义还不止于此。

sentences.en: It says we want you to join us.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 它是在说：我们希望你加入我们。

sentences.en: We want to share with you our cognitive secrets, our way of thinking about the world and how we solve problems.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们希望与你分享认知的奥秘，分享我们理解世界的思维方式，以及我们如何解决问题。

sentences.en: We want to count you as one of us.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们希望把你看作我们中的一员。

sentences.en: In doing that, it both holds out the promise of affiliation, connecting with others is a big motivator and the promise of greater competency with challenging tasks, not competency in being a kid or a student.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这样一来，它既让学生有机会获得归属感——与他人建立联系是很大的动力——也让学生有望提高处理挑战性任务的能力；这里说的，并不是更会做孩子或更会当学生。

sentences.en: But competency in being successful with the kinds of things that adults do.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 而是更有能力成功完成成年人所做的那些事情。

sentences.en: What about assessment?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 那么，评价方面呢？

sentences.en: How do we test disciplinary literacy?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我们该怎样测评学科读写素养？

sentences.en: There aren’t any standardized disciplinary reading or writing tests yet, but one can easily imagine how classroom assessments could change in the future as instruction becomes more disciplinary in focus.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 目前还没有标准化的学科阅读或写作测试；但很容易想象，随着教学更加侧重学科特点，未来课堂测评的方式也会发生变化。

sentences.en: Past assessments in history, literature or science have aimed to find out if students had mastered particular information.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 过去，历史、文学或科学方面的测评，旨在考查学生是否掌握了特定知识。

sentences.en: Questions about content would certainly still have a place in disciplinary literacy.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 在学科读写素养的测评中，考查内容知识的问题当然仍会占有一席之地。

sentences.en: Since knowledge matters in disciplinary literacy too.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 因为在学科读写素养中，知识同样重要。

sentences.en: But what would a more disciplinary assessment look like?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 但更加体现学科特点的测评，又应该是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: I think a more disciplinary assessment would seek to find out whether students are interpreting such information in a sophisticated way.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我认为，这种测评会考查学生能否以成熟深入的方式解读这些信息，

w.m: adj.成熟深入的；复杂精细的

sentences.en: According to the traditions of that discipline.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 并遵循该学科的传统方法。

sentences.en: For example, a disciplinary test in history might ask not only what we know about a historical event, but how we know about it.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 例如，历史学科的测评不仅会问，我们了解某个历史事件的哪些内容，还会问，我们是怎样了解它的。

sentences.en: Students would be questioned about the source of the information, the reliability of the source and how the information matches with information from other sources.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 学生需要回答信息来自哪里、来源是否可靠，以及它与其他来源的信息是否相符。

sentences.en: In cases where the information is contradictory, the assessment might ask students to determine whose account was more credible.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 当信息相互矛盾时，测评可能会要求学生判断，谁的叙述更可信，

sentences.en: Requiring students to weigh evidence using the same kinds of criteria that historians use.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 并要求学生运用历史学家所使用的同类标准来权衡证据。

sentences.en: Mm, that sounds interesting.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来很有意思。

sentences.en: Or a literature assessment might ask students to engage in deeper interpretation than in the past.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 或者，文学测评可能会要求学生比以往作出更深入的解读。

sentences.en: Instead of asking about the theme of a story, for example, an assessment might ask students to determine alternative themes, and to decide based on text evidence, which one the author seemed most sympathetic to.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 例如，它不只是询问故事的主题，而会要求学生找出其他可能的主题，并根据文本证据判断作者似乎最认同哪一种。

sentences.en: In other words it would ask the student to participate in the reading more as a literary critic than a student.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 换句话说，它要求学生更像文学评论家那样参与阅读，而不只是像学生那样阅读。

sentences.en: How should we prepare teachers to teach disciplinary literacy in teacher training institutions?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 在教师培养机构中，我们应该如何为教师教授学科读写素养作准备？

sentences.en: So far teacher training institutions haven’t done a very good job of helping subject matter teachers understand the discourse practices of their disciplines, so those practices often remain implicit, untaught.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，教师培养机构在帮助学科教师理解本学科的话语实践方面，做得还不够好；因此，这些实践往往仍隐而不显，也没有得到明确传授。

sentences.en: I agree with that, but have you seen any good examples?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点，不过你见过什么好的例子吗？

sentences.en: Sure, there are some examples of programs that do make disciplinary literacy practices explicit.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 当然，有一些培养项目确实明确呈现了学科读写素养的实践方式。

sentences.en: The best of these programs, in my opinion, are the result of literacy and disciplinary experts collaborating to determine what these practices are and then engaging students in them......
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在我看来，其中最好的项目，是读写教育专家与学科专家共同合作的成果：他们一起确定这些实践是什么，再引导学生参与其中。

sentences.en: This is the end of the second interview.
sentences.zh: 第二段访谈到此结束。
sentences.asr_text: This is the end of the second interview.

sentences.zh: 第8题：更加体现学科特点的测评会要求学生做什么？
